author: TEDx Talks
description:
Lia opens up about her life as a transgender athlete. Living your authentic life can seem impossible when parts of yourself seem incompatible, but when they’re allowed to coexist the result is joy unlike anything else. Lia Thomas (she/her) is a transgender woman, an athlete, and an advocate. 

She graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 2022 where she competed as an openly transgender swimmer and became the first trans athlete to win an NCAA D1 Championship. She received significant media attention for her competition on the women’s team and has spoken about her experiences and of the importance of inclusion in athletics. In addition to her NCAA awards, she has been named one of the 100 most Influential Philadelphians in 2022 and The Trustee’s Council of Penn Women’s 2022 Athletic Achievement Award. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The real story of a trans athlete | Lia Thomas | TEDxBoulder

description:
How many of us are waiting for the “perfect time” to truly begin?
The perfect plan. The perfect version of ourselves. The perfect moment.

In this deeply relatable and introspective talk at TEDxBITJaipur, Dr. Monica Bhatia explores the idea of “living in draft mode” — a state where we postpone action, delay expression, and hold back our authentic selves because we feel we are not ready yet.

We edit our dreams. We soften our opinions. We wait for confidence before we take the leap. But what if life was never meant to be a final version? What if growth happens precisely because we show up imperfectly?

Dr. Bhatia gently challenges the fear of imperfection and the illusion of readiness. Through thoughtful insights and real-life reflections, she encourages us to move from hesitation to participation — to stop endlessly revising our lives and start living them fully.

title: Living in draft mode | Dr. Monica Bhatia | TEDxBIT Jaipur

description: "Witches, Vampires, and Facism" explores common themes in what we today consider atrocities in history. It seeks to explore how circumstance can make witchhunters and fascists out of ordinary people, and how we are still haunted by those same circumstances today. Jason Lin is a junior at Moorestown Friends School. In his free time, he likes reading novels, learning about history, and doing theatre. Some of his favorite books are Six Of Crows, Scythe, Song of Achilles, and Sunrise On the Reaping. He also likes listening to the Crane Wives and Madilyn Mei’s music. His talk will focus on the history of scapegoating as well as its psychological roots. It will seek to explore much of the why behind atrocities like fascism and the Salem Witch Trials, and how they still haunt all of us even today. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Witches, vampires, and fascism | Jason Lin | TEDxMoorestown Friends School

In a world that never stops changing, waiting for clarity can quietly cost us time, confidence, and momentum. In this talk, Arya Agarwal challenges the idea that we must first find ourselves before we act.

Drawing on insights from neuroplasticity and lived experience, she reframes identity as something we train through behaviour - not something we discover through waiting. By combining intentional exposure, self-compassion, and reflection, she demonstrates how growth becomes a repeatable practice rather than a moment of inspiration.

Through a practical behavioural framework, she shows that readiness doesn’t precede action - it follows it. The message is precise and empowering: you don’t find yourself by waiting; you train yourself into who you’re becoming. This talk explores what viral internet trends like “6–7” reveal about how young minds experience attention, stimulation, and belonging in a digital-first world. Drawing from years of hands-on work with Gen Z and Gen Alpha students, Shirish examines how short-form content reshapes focus—not through speculation, but through observable behavioral patterns seen in learning environments.

Rather than framing technology as the enemy, this talk highlights four human-centered practices—clarity, consistency, coaching, and community—that educators and parents have found effective in helping young people regain agency, motivation, and purpose. Shirish Gupta is an award-winning youth mentor, TEDx speaker, and career strategist dedicated to empowering the next generation with mindset mastery and purpose-driven action. With deep experience guiding students on career planning, personal development, and life-ready skills using proven coaching frameworks, Shirish has advised thousands of young learner
title: What ‘6–7’ Reveals About Minds of Today’s Teens | Shirish Gupta | TEDxBHIS Kanpur Youth

description:
An Innovative Style of Leadership in Aa AI Powered World

For nearly 200 years, the world has been led by a single dominant model of leadership—Leading from the Front.
This model emerged during the Industrial Revolution, when mass production outpaced local markets. To address this challenge, industrial revolution pioneers turned to two powerful institutions for inspiration—the Church and the Military—and chose the military.
The military offered a clear template—an all-knowing, all-powerful General, supported by a rigid command-and-control structure, which ensured that orders issued were obeyed. Corporations mirrored this model, with the CEO replacing the General.
For generations, this model worked effectively—until Industry 4.0 (IR4) arrived. Powered by AI, it triggered three tectonic shifts:
• An explosion and democratization of data, making it impossible for any one person to “know it all”
• Unprecedented uncertainty, volatility, and disruption, rendering rigid command & control str
title: Leading From The Back | Rajesh Srivastava | TEDxBHIS Kanpur Youth

description:
When we hear the word intelligence or cognition, we instinctively picture human brains or perhaps advanced machines trained to imitate us humans. But what if intelligence is far older, far more distributed, and far more fundamental to life itself?

I would explore the idea of how intelligence or cognition is not confined to brains, but it emerges wherever living systems communicate, adapt, and make decisions. Drawing from my own research on learning and decision-making in organisms like pond snails, alongside work by other leading scientists, I will show how organisms without brains or even neurons solve problems, remember past experiences, and make flexible decisions. By expanding how we define intelligence, this perspective reshapes how we think about innovation in artificial intelligence. Instead of centralized control, nature offers models of distributed, resilient, and adaptive intelligence where systems learn to coordinate without commands.

title: IntelligenceEverywhere:RethinkingMindsBeyondBrains | Dr. Anuradha Batabyal | TEDxBHIS Kanpur Youth

The talk shares how Manan's own path was affected by two such events:
Public Speaking: Joining a Gavel Club in 2019 
Innovation: Developing AstroBott, an AI stargazing app, led to university incubation and receiving the Defence Minister Commendation Card in 2025.

Through Manan's initiative, ASTRA, he aims to bridge this gap by providing access to science and hands-on empowerment for underserved students. description:
In moments of pressure — during exams, difficult conversations, or overwhelming responsibilities — our minds often spiral into anxiety, fear, self-doubt, and stress. We are taught to “push through,” to suppress what we feel, and to keep moving. But what if the chaos within us isn’t a weakness to eliminate — but a signal to understand?

This talk explores the powerful idea that emotions are not enemies, but intelligent messengers. Anxiety signals that something matters. Fear prepares us for growth. Sadness honors what was meaningful. Anger protects what feels important. When we stop labeling emotions as negative and start listening to them as guidance, the chaos begins to soften.

Through reflection and practical insight, this session invites students, parents, and teachers to pause, listen, and respond differently to their inner world. Because clarity doesn’t come from silencing emotions — it comes from understanding them.
